'''Harry Leonard Swinney''' (April 10, 1939 – July 13, 2026) was an American physicist noted for his contributions to the field of [[nonlinear dynamics]].

==Early life and education==
Harry Leonard Swinney was born in [[Opelousas, Louisiana]], on April 10, 1939. His parents were Leonard R. Swinney and Ethel Bertheaud Swinney.<ref name="Reference-1">{{Cite Q|Q141895878}}</ref>

Swinney attended elementary school in Austin, Texas, and in 1957 graduated from Homer [[Louisiana]] High School. In 1961 he was awarded a B.S. with honors in physics by Southwestern at Memphis (now Rhodes College), where he was inspired by his physics professor and research mentor, Jack H. Taylor.  In 1968 he was awarded a Ph.D. in physics by Johns Hopkins University; his advisor was [[Herman Z. Cummins]].<ref name="Reference-1" />

==Career==
Swinney was an assistant professor of physics at New York University (1971–73) and was associate professor and then professor at the City College of the City University of New York (1973–78). Since 1978 Swinney joined the faculty of the University of Texas at Austin, where he became the Sid W. Richardson Foundation Regents Chair of Physics and director of the Center for Nonlinear Dynamics. He became a professor emeritus in 2018.<ref name="Reference-1" />

==Personal life and death==
In 1967 Swinney married Gloria T. Luyas, and in 1978 they had a son, Brent Luyas Swinney. Brent died of cancer in 1995, and Gloria died of cancer in 1997. He then married Lizabeth Kelley on August 12, 2000.

Swinney died at home in [[Austin, Texas]], on July 13, 2026, at the age of 87.<ref>{{cite web |title=Harry Swinney |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/statesman/name/harry-swinney-obituary?id=61982186 |website=Legacy |access-date=17 July 2026}}</ref><ref name="Reference-1" />

==Honors==
Swinney was a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] (1992) and a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (1977), the American Academy of Arts and Sciences (1991), the American Association for the Advancement of Science (1999), and the Society for Industrial and [[Applied mathematics|Applied Mathematics]] (2009). He was awarded the American Physical Society Fluid Dynamics Prize (1995), the Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics [[Jürgen Moser]] Prize (2007), the [[European Geosciences Union]] Richardson Medal (2012), and the Boltzmann Medal (2013) of the Commission on Statistical Physics of the International Union of Pure and Applied Physics. He was a Guggenheim Fellow (1983–84) and he was inducted into The Johns Hopkins University Society of Scholars (1984). He was awarded honorary doctoral degrees by Rhodes College (2002), The [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] (2008), and the [[University of Buenos Aires]] (2010).

==Research contributions==
Swinney conducted research on instabilities, chaos, and [[pattern formation]] in diverse systems, including fluid, chemical, and granular media. Swinney together with his students, postdocs, and other collaborators:  
*determined the decay rate of order parameter fluctuations for fluids near the critical point <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Swinney | first1=H. L. | last2=Cummins | first2=Herman Z. | title=Thermal Diffusivity of CO<sub>2</sub> in the Critical Region | journal=Physical Review | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=171 | issue=1 | date=1968-07-05 | issn=0031-899X | doi=10.1103/physrev.171.152 | pages=152–160| bibcode=1968PhRv..171..152S }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Swinney | first1=Harry L. | last2=Henry | first2=Donald L. | title=Dynamics of Fluids near the Critical Point: Decay Rate of Order-Parameter Fluctuations | journal=Physical Review A | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=8 | issue=5 | date=1973-11-01 | issn=0556-2791 | doi=10.1103/physreva.8.2586 | pages=2586–2617| bibcode=1973PhRvA...8.2586S }}</ref>
*observed a transition to chaos—deterministic yet nonperiodic behavior—in experiments on a fluid flow <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Gollub | first1=J. P. | last2=Swinney | first2=Harry L. | title=Onset of Turbulence in a Rotating Fluid | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=35 | issue=14 | date=1975-10-06 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.35.927 | pages=927–930| bibcode=1975PhRvL..35..927G }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Fenstermacher | first1=P. R. | last2=Swinney | first2=Harry L. | last3=Gollub | first3=J. P. | title=Dynamical instabilities and the transition to chaotic Taylor vortex flow | journal=Journal of Fluid Mechanics | publisher=Cambridge University Press (CUP) | volume=94 | issue=1 | date=1979-09-11 | issn=0022-1120 | doi=10.1017/s0022112079000963 | pages=103–128| bibcode=1979JFM....94..103F | s2cid=14359747 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Brandstater | first1=A. | last2=Swinney | first2=Harry L. | title=Strange attractors in weakly turbulent Couette-Taylor flow | journal=Physical Review A | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=35 | issue=5 | date=1987-03-01 | issn=0556-2791 | doi=10.1103/physreva.35.2207 | pages=2207–2220| pmid=9898397 | bibcode=1987PhRvA..35.2207B }}</ref>
*characterized chaos from time series data by computing the largest [[Lyapunov exponent]] (rate of loss of predictability)<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Wolf | first1=Alan | last2=Swift | first2=Jack B. | last3=Swinney | first3=Harry L. | last4=Vastano | first4=John A. | title=Determining Lyapunov exponents from a time series | journal=Physica D: Nonlinear Phenomena | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=16 | issue=3 | year=1985 | issn=0167-2789 | doi=10.1016/0167-2789(85)90011-9 | pages=285–317| bibcode=1985PhyD...16..285W | s2cid=14411384 | url=https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-01654059/file/AWJB.pdf }}</ref> and the [[mutual information]] (general dependence of two variables)<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Fraser | first1=Andrew M. | last2=Swinney | first2=Harry L. | title=Independent coordinates for strange attractors from mutual information | journal=Physical Review A | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=33 | issue=2 | date=1986-02-01 | issn=0556-2791 | doi=10.1103/physreva.33.1134 | pages=1134–1140| pmid=9896728 | bibcode=1986PhRvA..33.1134F }}</ref>
*discovered multiple transitions to different patterns of fluid flow between concentric independently rotating cylinders <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Andereck | first1=C. David |author1-link=C. David Andereck | last2=Liu | first2=S. S. | last3=Swinney | first3=Harry L. | title=Flow regimes in a circular Couette system with independently rotating cylinders | journal=Journal of Fluid Mechanics | publisher=Cambridge University Press (CUP) | volume=164 | year=1986 | issn=0022-1120 | doi=10.1017/s0022112086002513 | pages=155–183| bibcode=1986JFM...164..155A | s2cid=122768769 }}</ref>
*designed a laboratory experiment that yielded a stable vortex for conditions mimicking those on Jupiter.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Sommeria | first1=Jöel | last2=Meyers | first2=Steven D. | last3=Swinney | first3=Harry L. | title=Laboratory simulation of Jupiter's Great Red Spot | journal=Nature | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=331 | issue=6158 | year=1988 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/331689a0 | pages=689–693| bibcode=1988Natur.331..689S | s2cid=39201626 }}</ref> This result provides a plausible explanation of the stability of Jupiter's Great Red Spot, which was first observed by [[Robert Hooke]] in 1664.
*observed the emergence of a spatial pattern in a chemical system,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Ouyang | first1=Q. | last2=Swinney | first2=Harry L. | title=Transition from a uniform state to hexagonal and striped Turing patterns | journal=Nature | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=352 | issue=6336 | year=1991 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/352610a0 | pages=610–612| bibcode=1991Natur.352..610O | s2cid=4316122 }}</ref> as predicted in 1952 by [[Alan Turing]]
*determined the scaling of power dissipated in strongly turbulent flow between concentric rotating cylinders <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Lathrop | first1=Daniel P. | last2=Fineberg | first2=Jay | last3=Swinney | first3=Harry L. | title=Transition to shear-driven turbulence in Couette-Taylor flow | journal=Physical Review A | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=46 | issue=10 | date=1992-11-01 | issn=1050-2947 | doi=10.1103/physreva.46.6390 | pages=6390–6405| pmid=9907951 | bibcode=1992PhRvA..46.6390L }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Lewis | first1=Gregory S. | last2=Swinney | first2=Harry L. | title=Velocity structure functions, scaling, and transitions in high-Reynolds-number Couette-Taylor flow | journal=Physical Review E | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=59 | issue=5 | date=1999-05-01 | issn=1063-651X | doi=10.1103/physreve.59.5457 | pages=5457–5467| pmid=11969525 | bibcode=1999PhRvE..59.5457L }}</ref>
*observed [[anomalous diffusion]] and Lévy flights in a fluid flow <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Solomon | first1=T. H. | last2=Weeks | first2=Eric R. | last3=Swinney | first3=Harry L. | title=Observation of anomalous diffusion and Lévy flights in a two-dimensional rotating flow | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=71 | issue=24 | date=1993-12-13 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.71.3975 | pages=3975–3978| pmid=10055122 | bibcode=1993PhRvL..71.3975S }}</ref>
*discovered localized structures, dubbed "oscillons", in an oscillating granular layer;<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Umbanhowar | first1=Paul B. | last2=Melo | first2=Francisco | last3=Swinney | first3=Harry L. | title=Localized excitations in a vertically vibrated granular layer | journal=Nature | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=382 | issue=6594 | year=1996 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/382793a0 | pages=793–796| bibcode=1996Natur.382..793U | s2cid=4338010 }}</ref> oscillons were subsequently found in many dynamical systems.  The granular experiments also investigated various extended spatial patterns,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Melo | first1=Francisco | last2=Umbanhowar | first2=Paul B. | last3=Swinney | first3=Harry L. | title=Hexagons, Kinks, and Disorder in Oscillated Granular Layers | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=75 | issue=21 | date=1995-11-20 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.75.3838 | pages=3838–3841| pmid=10059744 | arxiv=patt-sol/9507003 | bibcode=1995PhRvL..75.3838M | s2cid=30000930 }}</ref> shock waves,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Rericha | first1=Erin C. | last2=Bizon | first2=Chris | last3=Shattuck | first3=Mark D. | last4=Swinney | first4=Harry L. | title=Shocks in Supersonic Sand | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=88 | issue=1 | date=2001-12-17 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.88.014302 | article-number=014302| pmid=11800951 | arxiv=cond-mat/0104474 | bibcode=2001PhRvL..88a4302R | s2cid=16876943 }}</ref> and fluctuations.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Schröter | first1=Matthias | last2=Goldman | first2=Daniel I. | last3=Swinney | first3=Harry L. | title=Stationary state volume fluctuations in a granular medium | journal=Physical Review E | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=71 | issue=3 | date=2005-03-30 | issn=1539-3755 | doi=10.1103/physreve.71.030301 | page=030301(R)| pmid=15903397 | arxiv=cond-mat/0501264 | bibcode=2005PhRvE..71c0301S | s2cid=8469315 }}</ref> 
*observed resonant pattern formation with frequency locking in chemical systems <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Petrov | first1=Valery | last2=Ouyang | first2=Qi | last3=Swinney | first3=Harry L. | title=Resonant pattern formation in achemical system | journal=Nature | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=388 | issue=6643 | year=1997 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/41732 | pages=655–657| bibcode=1997Natur.388..655P | s2cid=4394770 | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Masel/ko | first1=J. | last2=Swinney | first2=Harry L. | title=Complex periodic oscillations and Farey arithmetic in the Belousov–Zhabotinskii reaction | journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=85 | issue=11 | year=1986 | issn=0021-9606 | doi=10.1063/1.451473 | pages=6430–6441| bibcode=1986JChPh..85.6430M }}</ref>
*found fractal cascades of waves on the edges of leaves, flowers, and garbage bags <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Sharon | first1=Eran | last2=Roman | first2=Benoît | last3=Marder | first3=Michael | last4=Shin | first4=Gyu-Seung | last5=Swinney | first5=Harry L. | title=Buckling cascades in free sheets | journal=Nature | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=419 | issue=6907 | year=2002 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/419579a | page=579| pmid=12374967 | hdl=10533/173399 | s2cid=4419167 | hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Sharon | first1=Eran | last2=Marder | first2=Michael | last3=Swinney | first3=Harry | title=Leaves, Flowers and Garbage Bags: Making Waves | journal=American Scientist | publisher=Sigma Xi | volume=92 | issue=3 | year=2004 | issn=0003-0996 | doi=10.1511/2004.47.932 | pages=254–261|jstor=27858394}}</ref>
*found a resonance in internal wave boundary currents generated by tidal flow on a slope; this resonance apparently selects the angle (typically three degrees) of the continental slopes of the oceans <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Zhang | first1=H. P. | last2=King | first2=B. | last3=Swinney | first3=Harry L. | title=Resonant Generation of Internal Waves on a Model Continental Slope | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=100 | issue=24 | date=2008-06-20 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.100.244504 | article-number=244504| pmid=18643589 | bibcode=2008PhRvL.100x4504Z }}</ref> 
*discovered a new protein, Slf, which is produced by neighboring colonies of Paenibacillus dendritiformis bacteria.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Be'er | first1=A. | last2=Zhang | first2=H. P. | last3=Florin | first3=E.-L. | last4=Payne | first4=S. M. | last5=Ben-Jacob | first5=E. | last6=Swinney | first6=H. ==Other==
Swinney, together with Rajarshi Roy and Kenneth Showalter, founded a two-week ''Hands-On Research in Complex System'' ''Schools'' for early career scientists from developing countries in 2008. The schools, sponsored by the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]], have taught over 700 alumni from around the world.<ref name="Reference-1" />
